title: Steve Reeves was LYING about being natural?! (nattyornot.com)
summary: An unscripted rebuttal of a nattyornot.com article claiming Steve Reeves used steroids. He argues steroid availability in the 1940s is a fallacy, the Sergio Oliva quote contradicts itself, and pre-steroid physiques prove such bodies are natural; doubting natural icons only lowers lifters' standards.
claims: Steve Reeves built a lean, muscular, balanced physique when bodybuilding was in its infancy and is a goal physique for many naturals
The nattyornot.com author argues in bad faith out of envy, having failed to build such a physique himself
Even if Reeves had used drugs, a physique that doesn't look enhanced can be matched naturally by outworking drug users, many of whom are lazy and use drugs to replace work
Skepticism about historical natural physiques damages lifters by lowering their standards
Discovery of steroids in the 1930s and human trials from 1937 do not mean a bodybuilder had access by 1947; clinical trials do not equal everyday availability, especially without the internet
The earliest confirmed athletic testosterone use was Soviet weightlifters around 1954, so it is implausible a small-time US bodybuilder had access before the Soviet state
1940s testosterone preparations were crude and mostly raised aggression rather than muscle
Bill Pearl and a contemporary said they had to resort to veterinary products in the 1950s, a decade after Reeves' prime
Massive drug use is certain from the 1960s-70s; most 1950s physiques look naturally achievable

Sergio Oliva's quote that Arnold was among the first to bring steroids to America while listing Reeves contradicts itself; Reeves competed in the 1940s-50s and Oliva was about nine at Reeves' last contest
Steroid rumors about Reeves likely spread through jealous competitors and a game of telephone
Reeves may have experimented later, around his Hercules film years, but the young beach physique people aspire to was natural
Reeves was 6 ft 1 at about 215 lb; a lifter of that height can realistically get close to his look naturally
The article claims Reeves' softness came from testosterone water retention, while the same author dismisses pre-testosterone strongmen like Sandow as having doctored photos
Old-school Indian bodybuilders of the 1910s-1920s, with no drugs or modern information, had better physiques than many natural bodybuilders today
Testosterone was never developed for bodybuilding; science is rarely done for bodybuilders, and studies not designed for fitness (like EMG data) are often misapplied
